name: WCWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Raymond Chandler carried it through the whole of the promotion's own held early-2001 run before voluntarily vacating it at Total Anarchy 2001 to open an eight-man tournament; Dan Bonez won that tournament's final over Jason Myers to become the new champion.

name: WCWF International Television Championship
epitaph: Nathaniel Duke held it across the whole of the promotion's own held early-2001 run, defending it in a three-way, by disqualification and in a ladder match, until an in-ring explosion left him unable to continue the promotion's own invitational defense format at Total Anarchy 2001 and Jason Myers took the title by default.

name: WCWF United States Championship
epitaph: Insane Cain held it into the promotion's own 2001 run before the title went vacant for reasons the promotion's own surviving documents do not narrate; reinstated by owner Dick Hart, it produced a British Brawl four-corner match that ended in a simultaneous double pinfall, and Raziel Lucifer and JT Savage were ruled joint champions pending a decider the promotion's own surviving documents do not carry.

name: WCWF United States Tag Team Championship
epitaph: A retired set of belts owner Dick Hart brought back into circulation for one match at Total Anarchy 2001, where Derek Frost and Shawn's YB2K1 won them from Cold Steel.

name: WCWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Raymond Chandler and Jackson Therapy held it into the promotion's own 2001 run; by British Brawl the belts had passed, off the held record, to Salaok and Quartz's True Evil, whom Derek Frost and Shawn's YB2K1 then dethroned in that card's own tag title match.

name: WCWF Texas Championship
epitaph: The promotion's own surviving documents carry an unresolved contradiction: Ric Landell is billed the reigning Texas Champion at Total Anarchy 2001 (31 Mar), yet Jesse Helms is billed winning 'the WCWF's newest Texas Title' at British Brawl (8 Mar), three weeks earlier by the documents' own dates. Neither document narrates the other; both reigns are recorded as attested rather than resolved.

name: WCWF Hardcore Championship
epitaph: Dane Rennier won it at Saturday Storm in a multi-stage brawl the promotion's own broadcast narrates only in outline, and was still billed the champion three weeks later.

name: WCWF Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Eugene Whifflebottom held it into the promotion's own 2001 run; by Meltdown the belt had passed, off the held record, to Shawn, who carried it (once billed, likely in error, as a separate 'lightweight' title) through the rest of the promotion's own surviving documents.
